title: Bunk, the cigarette and Jim Robinson on lazy trumpeters
summary: Bunk put his horn down on purpose, and Jim Robinson complains of trumpeters who rest.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: No, I don't think that's contributing to this. What? Stop it. I mean, Bunk never considered it hard work that he'd have to be playing all the time. Sometime maybe when his lip wasn't always in shape, he didn't play all the time. Sometime he'd stop and light a cigarette in the middle. Some of the, even the record sessions, he sort of drops out in the middle of a chorus and people think, well, his lip got tired, he's an old man, he was 60 years old or something, and just worn out. And so he had to stop. But maybe what he did was stop and light a cigarette, you know, put his horn down for a minute and then pick it up whenever he wanted to. But if he were really feeling good and had confidence in all the players and knew that they all knew the tune and the way they were supposed to play it, well, he would be playing a second part and be filling in when some of the others were, taking solos, whatever you'd want to call them. But some of the records I made weren't that way all the way through. Occasionally he'd play all the way through a number, but usually he'd take off and let George Lewis take a chorus or so. But Jim would never stop, usually. And Jim, even today, complains bitterly when the trumpet puts his horn down quite often. Some certain players he'll refuse to play with regularly, say even at Preservation Hall, because they're too lazy, as he would say.
They don't play the lead? No, they just want to sit there and rest. Oh, I see. And Jim said, that's no way to do.
